analysis: The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. The visible diff is a date bump and one added troubleshooting table row (head line ~2555) about add-on hold behavior; the patch excerpt is truncated. The two examined units (head lines 806-1611) are unchanged surrounding documentation describing GLM serving, scheduling, calibration, deadlines and the prefix-cache flow. No code, config or control changes appear in the supplied evidence. The prose adds no new attack surface, and I did not observe claims that weaken stated mitigations. For example, the SSD prefix-cache description (T-041) matches the threat model: HMAC-keyed lookup, scope isolation, and the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch. The media text says media requests are excluded from prefix lookup and capture. The doc describes the per-donation gate only indirectly. The new add-on hold row relates to TB-012, A-018 and T-059. Only a truncated fragment was supplied and it is not in the primary units, so I could not verify its semantic accuracy, such as whether the hold is signature-checked or has lease/fallback semantics. The note that a load stops at its next check is operational documentation, not a control change. Remaining integration question: whether addon-hold.md and the real implementation match the row, and whether the doc drifts from T-059's assumptions. Nothing in the examined units supports a concrete finding.
